featured_reviews.name: Avinash Mehra
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had one of the worst experiences I’ve ever had at this pet store, and honestly I’m still upset thinking about it. From the moment I walked in, the place felt poorly maintained and depressing. The floors were dirty, there was a strong smell in the air, and the overall environment looked like it hadn’t been properly cleaned or cared for in a long time.

What really broke my heart, though, was seeing the kittens. There were about 15 kittens that looked barely two months old crammed into a single tiny cage. The cage was far too small for that many animals. They were all climbing over each other, scratching at the bars, and trying desperately to get out. Several of them looked extremely stressed and scared. Instead of playful, curious kittens like you’d expect, they just looked sad and uncomfortable. Watching them push against the cage door and meow was honestly heartbreaking.

It didn’t seem like they had enough space, stimulation, or proper care. The bedding looked dirty, and the whole setup felt more like storage than a place for living animals. Seeing such young kittens packed together like that made the entire experience feel really upsetting.

To make matters worse, everything in the store was wildly overpriced. Basic supplies that you can find elsewhere for reasonable prices were marked up way beyond what they should cost. When a store is already poorly maintained and clearly not prioritizing animal welfare, charging inflated prices just makes the whole thing feel even more frustrating.

The staff also didn’t seem particularly attentive or concerned about the animals. When I asked a question about the kittens, the response felt dismissive and rushed, as if my concerns weren’t important.

Between the overcrowded cages, the sad-looking kittens, the poor maintenance, and the ridiculous prices, this place left a really bad impression. A pet store should be a place where animals are treated with care and respect, not crammed into tiny cages and left in uncomfortable conditions.

I genuinely hope the store improves how it cares for its animals, because what I saw was really disappointing and upsetting. Until then, I would strongly recommend people look elsewhere for their pets and supplies.
Animals are living organisms with emotions not objects that you can treat however you want.I request you all to have a look and raise this issue,as a cat lover,this genuinely broke my heart.

Also I've been to the store many times and you never asked me my name so you can't say that when you reply.this is not a fake review.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
We are truly sorry that your visit left you feeling upset and disappointed. As animal lovers ourselves, the last thing we would ever want is for someone to walk away feeling that the animals in our care were unhappy or neglected.
We understand why the situation you witnessed with the kittens felt distressing, and we appreciate you taking the time to express your concerns. The kittens you saw had unfortunately been abandoned and were being temporarily housed together for their safety and care while we worked towards finding them permanent homes. Since we also have free roaming adult cats in the store, the enclosure was being used to prevent conflicts and injuries between the kittens and the older cats. The arrangement was temporary, and we’re happy to share that all of those kittens have now been successfully adopted into loving homes.
For the past five years, our mission at Drogo has always been centred around animal welfare, rescue, education, and responsible care. Beyond operating as a pet store, we actively support adoptions, rescue efforts, animal welfare awareness workshops for children, and even emergency medical cases that many others are unable to take on. Hundreds of rescued and abandoned animals have found homes through our efforts, often with us covering initial food, vaccinations, and veterinary support ourselves.
That said, we also understand that intent does not erase someone’s experience. Around the time of your visit, we were unfortunately facing a housekeeping staffing issue after an abrupt resignation, and the store was not presented at the standard we expect from ourselves. For that, we sincerely apologise. We have already taken steps to improve this.
Regarding the odour, while we do have ventilation and fresh air exchange systems installed, maintaining a completely odour free environment in a live animal facility can sometimes be challenging. Even so, we continuously work to improve cleanliness and comfort for both the animals and visitors.
As for pricing, we understand that our pricing may not always match larger wholesalers or high volume retailers. Operating a large fully air conditioned multi level facility with dedicated animal care infrastructure, veterinary support, and welfare initiatives does increase operational costs. However, we genuinely appreciate the feedback and are constantly working towards offering better value wherever possible.
We never want anyone to feel dismissed when raising concerns about animals, because caring deeply for them is exactly why Drogo was created in the first place. Many of our customers have supported us over the years because they have personally seen the work we do behind the scenes for rescues, rehabilitation, and responsible animal care and we are truly grateful to them.
We are sincerely sorry that your experience was not a positive one. As a small business deeply committed to rescue and animal care, every review impacts our ability to continue helping more animals in need.
